sections.label: Singapore athletes at Tokyo 2020
sections.summary: Singapore sent 23 athletes to the Olympics and 10 to the Paralympics, winning two gold medals and five national records.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: After a year of uncertainty and delays, we fielded our Team Singapore Olympians and Paralympians in Tokyo 2020 to compete with the world's best, to represent Singapore at the highest sporting showcase.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We sent a total of 23 athletes across 12 sports to the Olympics; 10 athletes across six sports to the Paralympics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Our athletes came home victorious with two gold medals and five national records, alongside numerous personal bests and many other personal inspiring stories.

sections.label: Debut sports and debutants
sections.summary: Singapore had athletes in Equestrian, Marathon Swimming and Diving for the first time, with 17 of 23 being Olympic debutants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For the first time, we had athletes represented in Equestrian, Marathon Swimming and Diving.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Of our 23-athlete strong contingent, 17 were Olympic debutants.

sections.label: Table tennis fourth place run
sections.summary: She finished fourth at the Olympics after beating two of four top-10 ranked table tennis players she was drawn against.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In her inspired run to fourth place at the Olympics, she was drawn against four of the world’s top 10 ranked table tennis players, she beat two of them along the way.

sections.label: Sailing pair in Medal Race
sections.summary: Kimberly and Cecilia became the first Singaporeans to compete in an Olympics Medal Race for sailing, racing all 12 Women's 49er FX races.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Kimberly and Cecilia made history as the first Singaporeans to ever compete in an Olympics Medal Race for sailing and they overcame great odds in all 12 of their races for the Women’s 49er FX, navigating not just unpredictable weather but also racing against much more experienced well-seasoned teams.

sections.label: Tandem cyclists' personal bests
sections.summary: Debutant tandem cyclist Steve and partner Kee Meng clocked two personal bests in the Men's B 1,000-metre Time Trial and 4,000-metre Individual Pursuit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Our debutant tandem cyclist Steve and his competition partner Kee Meng, they clocked two personal bests in the Men’s B 1,000-metre Time Trial and the Men’s B 4,000-metre Individual Pursuit.

sections.label: Diroy Noordin's shot put record
sections.summary: Flag-bearer Diroy Noordin threw 9.85 metres and then 9.92 metres in the men's F40 shot put final, breaking the national record both times.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Our contingent flag-bearer, Diroy Noordin, he left his mark on the field, quite literally.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: He threw a 9.85-metre and then 9.92-metre in the men’s F40 shot put final – he shattered the national record on both occasions.

sections.label: Pin Xiu's Paralympic swimming medals
sections.summary: She defended her S2 50-metre and 100-metre backstroke titles, winning the 100-metre by over nine seconds, totalling six medals across four Paralympic Games.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: These records continue to be unmatched, unbroken today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This year, she dominated the pool yet again, defending her title in the women’s S2 50-metre and 100-metre backstroke events, with some rather devastating performances.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: She won the 100-metre with a margin of more than nine seconds.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: That is a total of six medals, of which five are gold medals, across 13 years, over four Paralympic Games.

sections.label: Pin Xiu's 2008 Meritorious Service Medal
sections.summary: In 2008, Pin Xiu was awarded the Meritorious Service Medal for her accomplishments at the 2008 Beijing Paralympics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In 2008, Pin Xiu was awarded the Meritorious Service Medal for her accomplishments at the 2008 Beijing Paralympics.

sections.label: New President's Award for Inspiring Achievement
sections.summary: The Government intends to create a new President's Award for Inspiring Achievement, with Pin Xiu as inaugural recipient, recognising Singaporeans who overcame personal adversity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: My Cabinet colleagues and I discussed how we could appropriately recognise Pin Xiu’s achievements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: I am very happy to announce that we intend to create a new President’s Award for Inspiring Achievement, and to make the inaugural presentation of this award to Pin Xiu.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: President Halimah Yacob has agreed to this proposal.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This award will recognise Singaporeans who have overcome personal adversity and led inspiring lives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This prestigious award will be conferred by the President to deserving recipients who meet its highest qualifying criteria.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It will be presented to Singaporeans with fitting achievements and may not be given out every year.

sections.label: Personal best lift before Tokyo
sections.summary: She attained her personal best lift in her qualification event leading up to Tokyo, a performance of 77 kilogrammes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This paid off when she attained her personal best lift in her qualification event leading up to Tokyo.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It was a very credible performance of 77 kilogrammes.

sections.label: Government sports funding and commitment
sections.summary: The Government reiterates its commitment to supporting sports for all, growing the base and supporting elite athletes, investing about $70 million annually into the HPS system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: When you are out at sea, battling the winds, the waves and your opponents, for a few hours, this can make all the difference.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: So, Mr Speaker, at this juncture, let me reiterate the Government’s commitment to supporting and enhancing sports for all, both in growing the base, so that we can have more active participants and more athletes at the grassroots, and in supporting our elite athletes as they chase success on the podium at the world's best international events.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Government invests about $70 million annually into the HPS system.

sections.label: Supporting athletes and sporting culture
sections.summary: Each elite athlete is supported uniquely with differentiated, curated support, and the Government will continue working with sports stakeholders to build a cohesive sporting culture.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Members could see from some of the examples I outlined earlier how we approach each elite athlete uniquely, differently and how we support them with differentiated, curated support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will also continue to work with our sports stakeholders in our ecosystem, from our schools to NSAs, SNOC, SNPC, ActiveSG as well as the private academies and clubs, working together to build a strong, cohesive, vibrant sporting culture in Singapore.

sections.label: Disability sports accessibility and participation
sections.summary: The Disability Sport Master Plan emphasises grassroots development, and eight inclusive ActiveSG Gyms and six inclusive swimming complexes exist, with all ActiveSG Gyms to be inclusive by 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It is not just about elite sport performance, but really about the difference that mere participation can make.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We must, therefore, do all we can to make disability sports more accessible and encourage even more participation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Disability Sport Master Plan places emphasis on grassroots development, encouraging more to take part in sport, lowering the barriers to entry and enhancing the resources to facilitate participation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We now have eight inclusive ActiveSG Gyms and six inclusive swimming complexes across the island.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: These facilities have been retrofitted with equipment like inclusive gym machines and pool wheelchairs to make it far more accessible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We are on track to making every single ActiveSG Gym an inclusive one by 2026.

sections.label: Trained disability sports supporters
sections.summary: To date, 2,800 coaches, educators, volunteers, staff and students are trained to support disability sports.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To date, 2,800 coaches, educators, volunteers, staff and students are trained to support disability sports in one way or another.

sections.label: Disability sport participation in 2016
sections.summary: In 2016, one in three persons with disabilities participated in a sport at least once a week.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In 2016, one in three persons with disabilities participated in a sport at least once a week.

sections.label: SNPC para-athlete cash awards
sections.summary: SNPC is working on enhancing the cash awards for para-athletes in major games.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: SNPC is working on enhancing the cash awards for para-athletes in major games.

sections.label: Inclusive society through sports
sections.summary: The House will keep fostering an inclusive society through sports and thanks Team Singapore athletes for their Tokyo 2020 performances, which inspired and united Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: So, Mr Speaker, we will continue to work hard to foster an inclusive society through sports where people of all abilities can come together to experience, play, socialise and if they are able to, to excel at the highest level in sports, and through this, to help Singapore and Singaporeans build deep social connections.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: But allow me to circle back to my original Motion for this House – to thank Team Singapore athletes for flying our flag so high and with such distinction at Tokyo 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: All of you in this Chamber today have put Singapore amongst the world's best.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We congratulate you for your exceptional performances, for your indomitable fighting spirit on the world stage.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Your accomplishments brought cheer and joy to our nation and lifted our spirits in, perhaps, one of the most trying and difficult periods in Singapore's history.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: More importantly, your efforts inspired and united Singaporeans from all walks of life as they tuned in to support your Paralympic and Olympic journey.

sections.label: Congratulating Tokyo 2020 sporting talents
sections.summary: The speaker congratulates and celebrates the achievements of all sporting talents at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics and Paralympic Games.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Today, I congratulate and celebrate the achievements of all our sporting talents at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics and the Paralympic Games.

sections.label: Sports-related initiatives funding since 2008
sections.summary: Since 2008, over $4.3 million has been contributed to sports-related initiatives to help Singapore become a sporting nation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In fact, since 2008, we have contributed over $4.3 million on various sports-related initiatives to help Singapore become a sporting nation.

sections.label: 2021 Year of Celebrating SG Women
sections.summary: MSF has dedicated 2021 as the Year of Celebrating SG Women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: How apt that this year, MSF has dedicated 2021 as the Year of Celebrating SG Women.

sections.label: Athletes' personal bests and national records
sections.summary: Even without winning, some athletes achieved personal bests and others set national records.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even in instances where they may have not won, some achieved personal bests, others set national records.

sections.label: Support not dependent on winning
sections.summary: Support for sportsmen and sportswomen should not depend on them having won medals or tournaments.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: More generally, we need to understand as a nation that our support for our sportsmen and sportswomen should not be dependent on them having won medals or tournaments.

sections.label: Malaysia Cup, Team Singapore, cash award debate
sections.summary: The national team did not always win the Malaysia Cup but was always supported, raising the debate on cash awards for Olympians versus Paralympians.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The national team did not always bring home the Malaysia Cup but I remember we were always proud of our then "Team Singapore".

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I thought it opportune to bring up the topic of a debate, or a controversy that some people have mentioned before on the difference between cash awards for medalled Olympians versus medalled Paralympians.

sections.label: MAP and AAA cash award schemes
sections.summary: The two cash award schemes for medalists are the Multi-Million Dollar Award Programme for Olympians and the Athlete Achievement Award for Paralympians.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The two cash awards schemes for medalists are the Multi-Million Dollar Award Programme (MAP) for the Olympians and then, the Athlete Achievement Award (AAA) for the Paralympians.

sections.label: MAP and Paralympian gold awards
sections.summary: Under the MAP, a gold-winning Olympian may win $1 million but not more for another gold, while a gold-winning Paralympian earns $200,000 each time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For instance, under the MAP, a gold-winning Olympian may win $1 million but will not get more if he scores another gold medal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For the Paralympians, a gold-winning Paralympian, on the other hand, will earn a $200,000 award each time he or she wins a gold.

sections.label: Call to review disability sports system
sections.summary: The speaker calls for the Government to facilitate reviewing and resourcing the High Performance Disability Sports system and widening sports participation and the talent pipeline.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In this regard, I call for the Government to weigh in, to facilitate the process to reimagine, to review and to resource not only the High Performance Disability Sports system but also to widen the sports participation, to widen the talent pipeline through greater sports participation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This is a happy occasion, but at another occasion, I shall ask for an update from the Minister to the Disability Sports Master Plan including the need for developing a dashboard and review of the structure and the system, so that there is parity in both form and substance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Singapore has adopted and ratified the United Nations Convention for the Rights of Persons with Disabilities to grant equal rights to the disabled.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Our country has moved decisively in the last decade or more to narrow the gap between persons of different abilities in the important realms of life, in education, healthcare, transport, employment.

sections.label: House honours Tokyo Olympians and Paralympians
sections.summary: The House formally honours and thanks the Olympians and Paralympians who did Singapore proud at the Tokyo Games.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Today, this House formally honour and thank the Olympians and Paralympians who did us so proud at the Tokyo Games.

sections.label: Athletes raised Singapore's standing
sections.summary: The athletes placed a small nation like Singapore on the world stage and helped the country punch above its weight.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: You have placed a small nation like ours on the world stage, you have helped our country punch way above our weight in this space.

sections.label: Pin Xiu's two Tokyo golds
sections.summary: Pin Xiu won two golds, and the nation sang the Majulah Singapura at the Tokyo Aquatic Centre as the flag flew high.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Never once did we lose sight of the target, and in the end, Pin Xiu won two golds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Two times, we, as a nation sang the Majulah Singapura at the Tokyo Aquatic Centre as we joined the world to watch our flag fly high.

sections.label: spexScholarship support and deferments
sections.summary: The spexScholarship provides enhanced financial and programme support for elite athletes, and because of deferments Singapore realised its first Olympic gold through Joseph Schooling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Pin Xiu is also a beneficiary of the spexScholarship, which many of our athletes here today are on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The spexScholarship provides an enhanced level of financial and programme support for Singapore’s elite athletes, enabling talented athletes to pursue their sporting careers longer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Because of these deferments, Singapore was able to realise its first Olympic gold, care of Joseph Schooling.

sections.label: Parasports inclusion and volunteer support
sections.summary: The speaker urges MCCY, SDSC and SNPC to develop parasports programmes, make facilities accessible for PWDs, and engage companies and volunteers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The important thing in life is not victory but combat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is not to have vanquished but to have fought well." In the spirit of equality, I would like to encourage MCCY to work closely with SDSC and SNPC to develop the ecosystem and programmes to enable PWDs to pursue sports participation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Even if Singapore has built world-class sports facilities, we have a ways to go in making these facilities accessible for PWDs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As the sports ecosystem relies heavily on donations, sponsorships and volunteers at all levels, I encourage MCCY and SportSG to engage Government-linked companies and MNCs to adopt our national sports associations by financially supporting their activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would also like to urge more volunteers to step forward, be trained and make an impact through sport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By doing so, I believe we can bridge the disparities between parasports and sports by creating opportunities for all and developing a more inclusive society, something deeply rooted in the values as a nation.

sections.label: Paralympic medals and Yip Pin Xiu
sections.summary: Singapore athletes won two Gold medals and broke five National Records, with Yip Pin Xiu winning two Golds at the Tokyo Paralympic Games.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Our athletes came home with two Gold medals and broke five National Records.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Our heartiest congratulations to our swimmer and also former Nominated Member of Parliament, Ms Yip Pin Xiu, for winning two Golds at Tokyo Paralympic Games and a total of five Paralympic Gold medals for Singapore since Beijing Paralympics in 2008.

sections.label: Sports Hub and government sports funding
sections.summary: The $1.3 billion Sports Hub opened in 2014, and the Government invests about $400 million annually in sports, including $70 million on High Performance Sports.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In 2014, the $1.3 billion Sports Hub with its state-of-the-art integrated facilities opened.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Annually, the Government invests some $400 million towards sports and sports development in Singapore, including $70 million on the High Performance Sports system to support the development of national athletes and national sports associations.

sections.label: Focusing on three or four sports
sections.summary: Three or four sports will be carefully identified to focus on, based on performance outcome rather than social community participation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Basing on past performances and future potential, we will have to carefully identify three or four sports to focus on, basing on performance outcome and not social community participation.

sections.label: SPEX Scholarship and SpexBusiness support
sections.summary: The SPEX Scholarship, launched in 2013, gives about 70 top-tiered national athletes a monthly stipend, while SpexBusiness offers career development support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The SPEX Scholarship was launched in 2013 to address this issue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: SportSG sponsors about 70 top-tiered national athletes with a monthly stipend so that they can train full-time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Separately, SpexBusiness is a network of companies from diverse industries which offers our national athletes various career development support, such as employment opportunities and workplace flexibilities.

sections.label: Sports participation and ActiveSG growth
sections.summary: Regular weekly sports participation grew from 42% in 2011 to 69% in 2020, and ActiveSG gained two million members since 2014.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The annual National Sports Participation Survey reports that regular participation of at least once weekly in sports and physical activity grew from 42% in 2011 to an all-time high rate of 69% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Since the launch of ActiveSG in 2014, they have garnered a membership base of two million and a visitorship of over 17 million every year to ActiveSG sport facilities and programmes before the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In Northwest CDC, the brisk walking club has membership of more than 60,000 walkers!

sections.label: Ipsos pandemic weight gain study
sections.summary: An Ipsos study of 500 respondents found 30% gained about five kilogrammes on average during the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: A recent study by marketing research company Ipsos showed that 30% of 500 respondents experienced an average increase of around five kilogrammes during the pandemic.

sections.label: Private sector athlete support programmes
sections.summary: Existing funding programmes and corporate initiatives support athletes, and a committee with private sector executives is proposed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Examples include funding from SportsSG, the One Team Singapore Fund, spexScholarship and also spexBusiness which tap on private sector support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I am also aware, for instance, that Deloitte has its own specially-curated programme, "Deloitte Ignite" which offers internship and employment opportunities for elite athletes, current and retired.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: These existing programmes have certainly assisted our athletes over the years but, Sir, I think we can do more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: We can invite senior executives from the private sector to sit in a committee, together with MCCY, to look at how we can better support our athletes holistically.

sections.label: Japan corporate athletes culture
sections.summary: Japanese corporations have hired elite athletes as full-time employees with flexible work-training schedules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Japan, for example, has a culture of "corporate athletes", where Japanese corporations have sometimes hired elite athletes as full-time employees with a flexible work-training schedule that is tailored to meet the athlete concerned.

sections.label: Support for TeamSG athletes
sections.summary: The speaker acknowledges insights on sports bodies, pledges private sector partnership and framework review, and congratulates TeamSG athletes including Yip Pin Xiu.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Your insights being in the system, showing us your view from the inside, understanding the different moving parts between Singapore National Olympic Council (SNOC), Singapore National Paralympic Council (SNPC), Singapore Disability Sports Council (SDSC), all the acronyms, coming together, really say a lot about the village and the support that we have as a village to ensure the successes of our athletes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We will take them on board and review them closely with SportSG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The reiteration that we will work with the private sector and that there is a lot of good that will come out of this partnership, as I have mentioned earlier in my opening speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I underscore the point that we will reimagine our spots framework to ensure that all levels of participation from the grassroots through to the elite sporting talents will be given opportunities through programmes like the spexScholarship and others to allow athletes to realise their full potential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: On this, let me come back to the Motion and reiterate our gratitude, our thanks and our deepest, warmest congratulations to all of our TeamSG athletes, Olympians, Paralympians and, in particular, our Gold Medalist champion from Tokyo 2020 and now five-time Gold Medal winner Paralympian, Ms Yip Pin Xiu on her award today.
